q: What are the three processes of the Schedule performance domain?
options: Define Activities, Sequence Activities, Control Schedule
Plan Schedule Management, Estimate Durations, Close Schedule
Plan Schedule Management, Develop Schedule, Monitor and Control Schedule
Develop Schedule, Validate Schedule, Report Schedule
explanation: The 8th edition has three Schedule processes. Defining, sequencing and estimating activities are steps inside Develop Schedule.
ref: PMBOK 8, Guide 2.3.2

q: What is the correct order of the four steps for developing the schedule?
options: Define activities, determine sequence, estimate effort and duration, adjust
Estimate effort and duration, define activities, determine sequence, adjust
Determine sequence, define activities, adjust, estimate effort and duration
Define activities, estimate effort and duration, adjust, determine sequence
explanation: First the activities are defined, then sequenced, then estimated, and finally the draft schedule is adjusted until it is acceptable.
ref: PMBOK 8, Guide Figure 2-23

q: What does the schedule management plan contain?
options: The start and finish dates of every activity
How the schedule will be developed, managed and controlled, including units of measure and control thresholds
explanation: The schedule management plan gives guidance on how the schedule will be managed: level of accuracy, units of measure, control thresholds, reporting formats. It contains no dates.
ref: PMBOK 8, Guide 2.3.2.1

q: Schedule activities are created by decomposing which of the following?
explanation: Define activities decomposes the work packages of the WBS into schedule activities, which are the basis for estimating, scheduling and controlling the work.
ref: PMBOK 8, Guide 2.3.2.2

q: What is the duration of a milestone?
options: The duration of the activity before it
It depends on the project calendar
explanation: A milestone is a significant point or event in the project, so it has zero duration.
ref: PMBOK 8, Guide section 4, Milestone list

q: Testing cannot start until coding has finished. Which logical relationship is this?
explanation: In a finish-to-start relationship the successor cannot start until the predecessor has finished. It is the most commonly used relationship.
ref: PMBOK 8, Guide section 5, Precedence diagramming method

links.label: PMBOK 8, Guide section 5, Precedence diagramming method

q: Which logical relationship is very rarely used?
explanation: Start-to-finish, in which the successor cannot finish until the predecessor has started, is very rarely used. Finish-to-start is the most common.
ref: PMBOK 8, Guide section 5, Precedence diagramming method; Practice Standard for Scheduling, 3.4.8

links.label: PMBOK 8, Guide section 5, Precedence diagramming method

q: Leveling the concrete cannot begin until pouring the foundation begins. Which relationship is this?
explanation: In a start-to-start relationship the successor cannot start until the predecessor has started.
ref: PMBOK 8, Guide section 5, Precedence diagramming method

links.label: PMBOK 8, Guide section 5, Precedence diagramming method

q: In the precedence diagramming method, how are activities shown?
options: As horizontal bars drawn against a time scale
As nodes, linked by logical relationships
explanation: The precedence diagramming method represents activities as nodes and links them with one or more logical relationships to show the sequence of work.
ref: PMBOK 8, Guide section 5, Precedence diagramming method

links.label: PMBOK 8, Guide section 5, Precedence diagramming method

q: After the concrete is poured, the team must wait three days for it to cure before building the walls. The three days are:
explanation: A lag is the amount of time a successor activity is delayed with respect to its predecessor. A lead advances the successor.
ref: PMBOK 8, Guide section 5, Leads and lags

links.label: PMBOK 8, Guide section 5, Leads and lags

q: Landscaping is scheduled to start two weeks before the punch list is complete. This is an example of:
explanation: A lead is the amount of time a successor activity can be advanced with respect to its predecessor. This is a finish-to-start relationship with a two-week lead.
ref: PMBOK 8, Guide section 5, Leads and lags

links.label: PMBOK 8, Guide section 5, Leads and lags

q: The walls cannot be built until the foundation is complete. What type of dependency is this?
explanation: Mandatory dependencies, also called hard logic, are legally or contractually required or inherent in the nature of the work, often because of physical limitations.
ref: PMBOK 8, Guide section 5, Dependency determination and integration

links.label: PMBOK 8, Guide section 5, Dependency determination and integration

q: The team decides to complete the plumbing before starting the electrical work because that is good practice, although both could be done in parallel. What type of dependency is this?
explanation: Discretionary dependencies, also called soft or preferred logic, are based on good practice where another sequence would also be acceptable.
ref: PMBOK 8, Guide section 5, Dependency determination and integration

links.label: PMBOK 8, Guide section 5, Dependency determination and integration

q: Early in a project, with very little detail available, the project manager estimates the duration from a similar project completed last year. Which technique is this?
explanation: Analogous estimating uses historical data from a similar activity or project. It is less costly and quicker than other techniques, but also less accurate.
ref: PMBOK 8, Guide section 5, Analogous estimating

q: A crew can install 25 meters of cable per hour and 1,000 meters must be installed. Using parametric estimating, how long will the work take?
explanation: Parametric estimating multiplies the quantity of work by the time per unit: 1,000 meters ÷ 25 meters per hour = 40 hours.
ref: PMBOK 8, Guide section 5, Parametric estimating

q: Which estimating technique adds up the estimates of the lower-level components of the WBS?
explanation: Bottom-up estimating aggregates the estimates of the lower-level components. It is the most detailed and the most time-consuming technique.
ref: PMBOK 8, Guide section 5, Bottom-up estimating

q: An activity has an optimistic estimate of 4 days, a most likely estimate of 6 days and a pessimistic estimate of 14 days. What is the expected duration using the triangular distribution?
explanation: Triangular distribution is a simple average: (4 + 6 + 14) ÷ 3 = 8 days.
ref: PMBOK 8, Guide section 5, Multipoint estimating; Practice Standard for Scheduling, 3.4.3

q: Using the same estimates (optimistic 4, most likely 6, pessimistic 14 days), what is the expected duration using the beta (PERT) formula?
explanation: The beta or PERT formula weights the most likely estimate four times: (4 + 4×6 + 14) ÷ 6 = 42 ÷ 6 = 7 days.
ref: Practice Standard for Scheduling, 3.4.3; PMBOK 8, Guide section 5, Multipoint estimating

q: What is the difference between effort and duration?
options: Effort is measured in days, duration in hours
Effort includes weekends, duration does not
Effort is the number of labor units required; duration is the number of work periods needed with the estimated resources
explanation: Effort is the labor units needed to complete the work. Duration is the number of work periods needed, which depends on how many resources are assigned.
ref: PMBOK 8, Guide 2.3.1

q: A manager doubles the number of people on an activity and expects it to take half the time, but it takes longer than planned. Which concept explains this?
explanation: Adding resources yields progressively smaller gains. Too many resources can even increase duration because of knowledge transfer, learning curves and extra coordination.
ref: PMBOK 8, Guide 2.3.2.2

q: What is rolling wave planning?
options: Planning all work in full detail at the start
Moving unfinished work to the next phase
Planning near-term work in detail and future work at a higher level
explanation: Rolling wave planning is an iterative technique: near-term work is planned in detail and later work at a higher level, to be detailed as more information becomes available.
ref: PMBOK 8, Guide section 5, Rolling wave planning

links.label: PMBOK 8, Guide section 5, Rolling wave planning

q: In a predictive project, how can the schedule baseline be changed?
options: Only through an approved change request, using integrated change control
By the project manager updating the scheduling tool
By the team at the daily meeting
explanation: Any change to the schedule baseline can only be approved through the Assess and Implement Changes process by applying integrated change control.
ref: PMBOK 8, Guide 2.3.2.3

q: In an adaptive project, what is velocity?
options: The number of team members per iteration
The speed at which change requests are approved
The rate at which deliverables are produced, validated and accepted per iteration
explanation: Velocity is the rate at which deliverables are produced, validated and accepted in the given time per iteration. It is used to track and forecast progress.
ref: PMBOK 8, Guide 2.3.2.3

q: In planning poker, why do all team members reveal their cards at the same time?
options: To save time in the meeting
So that no one's estimate is influenced by a number someone else said first
Because the product owner decides the estimate
So that the highest card always wins
explanation: Each member privately selects a card and all cards are revealed together. This avoids anchoring, where the first number mentioned pulls the other estimates toward it.
ref: Practice Standard for Project Estimating, 4.3; Practice Standard for Project Estimating, 4.5

q: Each team member quietly adds two extra days to every estimate "just in case". What is the result for the project schedule?
options: No effect at all, because the hidden additions cancel each other out
An oversized schedule, because the hidden buffers add up
explanation: Padding each estimate compounds across work packages and produces an oversized buffer. Uncertainty should be handled with a visible reserve instead.
ref: Practice Standard for Project Estimating, 4.5

q: A draft schedule shows an item called "Design approved" with a duration of five days. What should the scheduler change?
options: Nothing: every item in a schedule needs a duration
Extend it, because approvals usually take longer
Remove it from the schedule altogether, because approvals are never shown on a schedule
Make it a milestone of zero duration, with the review as a separate activity
explanation: A milestone is a significant point or event and has zero duration. The work of reviewing the design takes time and is an activity; the approval that ends it is the milestone.
ref: PMBOK 8, Guide section 4, Milestone list

q: A team could paint the walls before or after laying the carpet. From experience it prefers to paint first, and puts that order in the schedule. What kind of dependency is this?
explanation: A discretionary dependency is a preferred order based on good practice or experience, not on the nature of the work. It can be changed if the schedule needs compressing. A mandatory dependency is required by the work itself or by contract.
ref: PMBOK 8, Guide section 5, Dependency determination and integration

links.label: PMBOK 8, Guide section 5, Dependency determination and integration

q: Records show that a crew lays 20 meters of pipe a day. The project needs 400 meters. Using this rate, what is the duration, and which technique is it?
explanation: Parametric estimating uses a statistical relationship between historical data and other variables: 400 m ÷ 20 m a day = 20 days.
ref: PMBOK 8, Guide section 5, Parametric estimating

q: Match each example with the logical relationship between the two activities.
left: The operating system is installed after the hardware is assembled
Editing cannot finish until writing has finished
Leveling concrete cannot start until pouring has started
Delivery of equipment cannot finish until its installation has started
explanation: The first word is about the predecessor and the second about the successor. Finish-to-start: the successor starts after the predecessor finishes. Start-to-finish, the rarest, means the successor cannot finish until the predecessor has started.
ref: PMBOK 8, Guide section 5, Precedence diagramming method

links.label: PMBOK 8, Guide section 5, Precedence diagramming method

q: Match each example with the type of dependency.
left: The foundation must be built before the walls
Plumbing is finished before electrical work, by preference
Work waits for a government permit
explanation: A mandatory dependency comes from law, contract or the nature of the work. A discretionary one is a preferred order, although another would work. An external one depends on something outside the project.
ref: PMBOK 8, Guide section 5, Dependency determination and integration

links.label: PMBOK 8, Guide section 5, Dependency determination and integration

q: Which kind of dependency has the site lead described?

strip.says: Could we lay the cables before the walls are painted?
We could. No rule and no physical reason stops us.
We paint first because experience tells us it gives a cleaner result.

explanation: A discretionary dependency, also called soft or preferred logic, is an order chosen because it is good practice, although another order would work. A mandatory dependency comes from law, a contract or the nature of the work.
ref: PMBOK 8, Guide section 5, Dependency determination and integration

links.label: PMBOK 8, Guide section 5, Dependency determination and integration
